tex_content.html:
Proposition

↗ lem:6-2

1. ch6:6.3If $A$ is an open or closed subset of $\mathbb {R}^{n-1}$ or $\mathbb {H}^{n-1}$ and $f:A\to \mathbb {R}$ is continuous, then the graph of $f$ has measure zero in $\mathbb {R}^n$.

Proof

\sketch For compact $A$, argue by induction on $n$. The case $n=1$ is a set with at most one point. For each $c\in \mathbb {R}$, the slice of the graph in $\{ c\} \times \mathbb {R}^{n-1}$ is the graph of a continuous function of $n-2$ variables, hence is null by induction. Lemma 1 makes the entire graph null. In general, Proposition A.60 expresses $A$ as a countable union of compact sets, so its graph is a countable union of null sets.

□
